item.title: US sanctions Hezbollah-linked charity in push against Iran's proxies, Treasury says
item.description:
By Andrea Shalal

Nov 18 (Reuters) - The United States on Wednesday issued new Hezbollah-related sanctions targeting three people based in Lebanon, and three entities as part of a broader effort to shut down Iran's proxy networks, the Treasury Department said.

Treasury said its Office of Foreign Assets Control designated the Hezbollah-affiliated charity Ta’awanu Association and its founder, along with two Lebanese brothers who the US said have aided the Islamic militant group with a gold- and cash-smuggling network.

item.title: Threats from Iran have increased substantially, US intelligence director says
item.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Threats from Iran to Americans inside and outside the United States have increased substantially, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told lawmakers on Wednesday.

"We remain committed to detecting, deterring, and combating the Iranian lethal plotting outside the United States and inside the United States," Clayton said at a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing.

"These threats have substantially increased. Our women and men abroad, our women and men here in the United States, are under greater threat."

item.title: As criticism mounts, Trump administration says tech outages not coordinated
item.description:
By Doina Chiacu, Alexandra Alper and Mike Stone

WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the disruptions to critical systems over the past week were not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack, as President Donald Trump's administration faces mounting criticism over its response.

Technology-related disruptions have hit every weekday between Thursday and Tuesday, including a nationwide halt to air travel, aMicrosoft outage that hit email services and a temporary disruption to theUS National Security Agency's network.
